title: Some Roman doctors grant Jeroboam meant the true God—and still call the cult illicit, a blade that cuts today’s images too
source_text: XXXVII. Sed sunt inter Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae qui agnoscunt Jeroboam & Israelitas in vitulis verum Deum colere voluisse, & nihilominus eorum cultum fuisse illicitum & idololatricum: non quod vitulos pro Diis haberent, sed quod Deum colerent modo ab ipso non praescripto, & imaginibus adorarent quas ipse non instituerat. Quo argumento, fatentur, etiam hodiernum imaginum cultum, si Deus eum non approbet, eadem ratione damnari posse.
pass_a_gloss: But there are among the Doctors of the Roman Church who acknowledge that Jeroboam and the Israelites wished to cultivate the true God in the calves, and that nevertheless their cult was illicit and idolatrous: not because they held the calves for Gods, but because they cultivated God in a mode not prescribed by him, and adored with images which he himself had not instituted. By which argument, they confess, even today’s cult of images, if God does not approve it, can be condemned by the same reason.
pass_b_english: Honest Roman voices admit relative Jehovah-calf cult can still be idolatry—wrong mode, unauthorized images.
They concede the same knife can cut today’s image-cult if God has not approved it.

lemmas.gloss: in a mode not prescribed by him

choices.english: if God does not approve it
choices.why: Their conditional that threatens modern praxis.
